issues.title: [BUG] Minecraft doesn't fully exit on window close when Placebo and Steam 'n' Rails are both loaded on Linux
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
For some reason, when both Steam 'n' Rails and [Placebo](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/placebo) are loaded, exiting the game does not exit the game process, and it still shows up as running in Prism Launcher, forcing me to manually kill it. It doesn't happen if either mod is removed. This also seems to only happen on Linux, as my friends who I sent my modpack to don't have this problem.

**To Reproduce**
1. Install:
    - Minecraft [1.21.1]
    - Neoforge [21.1.233]
    - [Create](https://modrinth.com/mod/LNytGWDc) [6\.0\.10]
    - [Create: Steam 'n' Rails 1\.21\.1](https://modrinth.com/mod/L3Jv0QZI) [0\.2\.0\+neoforge\-mc1\.21\.1]
    - [Placebo](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/283644) [9\.9\.1]
2. Launch game
5. exit game
6. game still running

**Expected behavior**
The game should fully close when I close it.

**Additional context**
Minimal reproduction log (first time launch): https://mclo.gs/AornOPc

Here's what my clanker said about what it thinks is going on, hopefully it's at least somewhat helpful:
<details>
<summary>slopothesis</summary>

## Root Cause: Placebo's non-daemon threads block clean JVM shutdown

**Placebo's `TrailsManager.init()`** and **`WingsManager.init()`** each spawn threads via `new Thread(runnable, name).start()` **without calling `setDaemon(true)`**:

- `"Placebo Patreon Trail Loader"` - fetches `PatreonTrails.txt` from `raw.githubusercontent.com`
- `"Placebo Patreon Wing Loader"` - fetches `PatreonWings.txt` from `raw.githubusercontent.com`

These are **non-daemon (user) threads** by default. They do blocking HTTP/HTTPS I/O to GitHub. If the network request hangs (SSL handshake, DNS, GitHub rate limiting), the threads never complete.

### The deadlock chain

1. User closes Minecraft -> `Minecraft.stop()` -> `System.exit(0)` begins the JVM shutdown sequence
2. NeoForge/render mods' shutdown hooks start cleaning up: OpenGL context destruction, buffer deletions, etc.
3. A GL operation triggers a **safepoint** (for GC or class unloading)
4. The safepoint mechanism tries to suspend **all threads**, including Placebo's patreon loader threads
5. Placebo's threads are stuck in **native HTTP I/O** (inside `java.net.SocketInputStream.socketRead0`) - **cannot reach a safepoint** from native code
6. The VM Thread, coordinating the safepoint, enters the NVIDIA GL driver code (through thread stack inspection or resource tracking) and **hangs inside `libnvidia-glcore.so`**
7. The Render thread (stuck in `JVM_Halt` -> `VM_Exit` -> waiting for VM Thread) can never complete because the VM Thread is stuck in the driver
8. Non-daemon threads prevent the JVM from force-exiting via `halt()` - deadlock

### Why it only happens with Placebo + Steam 'n' Rails

Steam 'n' Rails' train inventory serialization during shutdown increases object allocation on the server thread. This allocation pressure triggers GC -> safepoint -> exposes the existing non-daemon thread issue from Placebo. Without Steam 'n' Rails, the server shutdown has less allocation pressure, the GC/safepoint might not trigger during the critical window, and the GL cleanup completes normally.

### What Placebo should do

Both thread creations need `setDaemon(true)` added **before** `start()` - or use `CompletableFuture.runAsync()` (which uses the daemon-threaded `ForkJoinPool.commonPool`). Since these are purely cosmetic data fetches (patreon wings/trails), there's no reason for them to be user threads.
</details>

issues.body:
**FYI:** Mostly a reminder than issue since these files are often forgotten to be updated.  There are files to change for 1.17.1 to work.
**mods.toml**, ***mixins*** and **pack.mcmeta** need updating for every major release of Minecraft depending on what is included.
Minecraft 1.17.x - Minimum Java Level Supported: 16.0.1
pack.mcmeta files Pack Format=7 for 1.17.x release, 6 for 1.16 and 5 for 1.15, etc.
Minecraft Vanilla Launcher (new one from Microsoft Store) has loading issues that require additional changes to our mods and modpacks.  Read conversation towards the bottom on Forge Support: https://forums.minecraftforge.net/topic/105079-forge-1171-not-launching/?_fromLogin=1
This describes how to workaround the breaking change Microsoft made with the new Vanilla Minecraft launcher.  I'm posting here as I've looked at this 1.17.x version of the mod and found one or both issues exist.  It wasn't an easy process figuring out why mods were not working properly so I've provided the data so you don't have to waste time trying to figure out why.

issues.title: [1.16.1] Mod removal prevents certain shapeless recipes from working on a world-by-world basis
issues.body:
This is a bit of a weird one, and is best demonstrated by example with Industrial Foregoing's dry rubber recipe. By default, the recipe works fine. You can take 9 tiny dry rubber and get 1 dry rubber, which you then use to make plastic. Adding FastWorkbench and Placebo, specifically, still works. However, adding BiomesOPlenty on top stops the dry rubber recipe from working, though it still shows up in the JEI.

I've tested 4 cases:
- Industrial Foregoing (and required dependency Titanium) alone **[works]**,
- Industrial Foregoing, Titanium, FastWorkbench, and Placebo **[works]**,
- Industrial Foregoing, Titanium, and BiomesOPlenty **[works]**,
- Industrial Foregoing, Titanium, BOP, FastWorkbench, and Placebo **[recipe fails]**

I used JEI in all 4 cases to confirm the recipe is somehow still registered (at least to it), but removing JEI doesn't change the behavior in each case. It's important to note that BOP nor Placebo are causing the issue, except when they're installed together.

This case persists even when using other workbenches, such as the Immersive Engineering treated workbench, or even the Refined Storage crafting patterns. This is all using the latest versions of the respective mods, and Forge 32.0.75. I've heard from others that recipes from Potions Master things also don't work, and that the OpenBlocks Elevator recoloring recipes create blue cheese from Rats (when installed), so I'll update the issue after checking forge versions and confirming these recipes as well.

Logs don't seem problematic. Here's the log for the server I've been using for testing, Placebo doesn't note any recipe issues: https://pastebin.com/cRYvbi2F

Also see https://github.com/InnovativeOnlineIndustries/Industrial-Foregoing/issues/807 where this issue was first reported.


Please let me know if this issue should be in the FastWorkbench repo instead, it's here because it seems to be a problem with the fast recipe registration.
